title: When the Spire Breaks
premise: Ansel Eriksen, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the ivory they leave behind, has spent their whole life in a valley where magic cannot follow—until a crown decree turns the gift into a death sentence and soldiers drag them beyond the valley's edge. Hunted alongside a disgraced dragon-warden and a runaway court scribe, Ansel learns their own soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain generations ago, which is why the dead speak to them and why the king's spire-mages want them alive. The trio descends to steal the soul back before the last dragon-fire—the only thing keeping the mountain court sealed—gutters out, discovering that the fire is dying because Ansel's stolen soul has been feeding it. In the climax, Ansel chooses to shatter the soul rather than reclaim it, freeing the dead, unmaking the hunt, and finding a family that chooses them without magic's help.
about_author: Noor Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funeral carvings in northern museum basements. They write fantasy about grief, inheritance, and the families we carve for ourselves.

chapters.title: Ivory Voices
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In the magicless valley, Ansel carves whalebone charms and quietly hears the dead who cling to them, hiding the gift even from their adoptive grandmother, Maren. A dying traveler's charm screams with a warning: the crown's spire-mages have begun a hunt. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a secret self, and the first crack in Ansel's safe, small life.

chapters.title: The Decree at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Crown soldiers seal the valley's only pass, demanding every resident submit to a bone-testing that would expose Ansel instantly. Maren burns her own charms to cover for them, but a soldier recognizes the carvings' signature. Ansel flees over the ridge—the first time magic can touch them—and it does, violently. Emotional beat: exile as both catastrophe and strange liberation.

chapters.title: The Warden of Embers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, meeting Sefa, a disgraced dragon-warden hiding in the border fens, the last keeper of a fire that is nearly out. Sefa recognizes what Ansel is: a 'hollow-boned,' someone whose soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain. She offers passage in exchange for Ansel's help reaching the mountain. Emotional beat: wary alliance; the first person who doesn't flinch at what Ansel is.

chapters.title: What the Scribe Stole
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. A runaway court scribe, Tobin carries stolen ledgers proving the hunt is a harvest: the spire-mages are collecting hollow-boned souls to feed the failing seal on the court below. Caught stealing rations, Tobin bargains their knowledge to Ansel and Sefa. Emotional beat: guilt and self-justification; Tobin's cowardice cracking into courage.

chapters.title: The Hunt on the White Road
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Spire-mages ambush the trio on the mountain road, using captured dead to sing Ansel's own soul-song back at them and paralyze them. Sefa spends a decade of her remaining dragon-fire to break the song, revealing how little of the fire is left. They escape into a dead village where Ansel hears hundreds of sold souls. Emotional beat: horror at the hunt's scale; resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Deciphering the ledgers in the ruined village, Tobin finds Ansel's name—sold by their own birth parents to buy the valley's protection—and learns Maren has known all along. Tobin must decide whether to tell Ansel, and confesses their own brother was harvested years ago. Emotional beat: the weight of inheritance; truth as an act of love.

chapters.title: Descent Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Guided by the dead of the village, the three enter the court beneath the mountain through a drowned mine. Inside, the spire's mages have built a throne of harvested souls, and Ansel's own soul sits at its heart, keeping the seal and the dying fire alive. Sefa is captured buying them time. Emotional beat: awe and dread; the found family fracturing under sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Court of Sold Souls
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Confronting the court's ancient steward, Ansel learns the choice offered to every hollow-boned: reclaim the soul and let the seal break, or leave it and live hollow forever while the harvest continues. The dead around them beg—some for freedom, some for the seal to hold. Emotional beat: the impossible arithmetic of one soul against many.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Spire
chapters.summary: Tobin and Sefa's interwoven climax. Tobin frees Sefa and torches the ledger-throne with the last of the dragon-fire, while Ansel, instead of reclaiming their soul, shatters it—releasing every harvested dead, collapsing the court, and ending the hunt's purpose. The mountain exhales. Ansel survives, hollow but whole in a new way. Emotional beat: self-erasure transformed into self-definition.

chapters.title: A Family Carved from Silence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The valley's magicless quiet now holds no fear—Ansel no longer hears the dead, and grieves and rejoices in the same breath. Sefa plants the fire's final ember in the valley's hearth; Tobin begins writing the true history. Maren welcomes them home. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—identity not as inheritance, but as choice; found family settling in like hearth-smoke.
